title: Dynamic impact drift: Mid-run conflict detection and bounded replanning
body:
<!-- factory-conflict-aware-scheduling-2026-11-01:child-8 -->
Parent epic: #192

## Objective
Reconcile declared impact with edits in progress and target branch evolution; avoid late integration surprises while protecting agent progress.
## Work
- [ ] Event triggers: new modified paths, contract changes, branch rebase/base SHA divergence, lease health, dependency reprioritization, human override, cancelled task.
- [ ] Incremental git diff and manifest-vs-actual comparison, severity thresholds and debounce; no repeated LLM planning for each edit.
- [ ] On conflict choose continue with tracked obligation, checkpoint/pause lower priority, await merge, bounded replan with changed files, or human decision; no silent unilateral code loss.
- [ ] Record remediation provenance, preserve worktree and local state when pausing; use existing #131 lifecycle and recovery.
- [ ] Cap iterations/cost, implement cooldown and idempotency, update predicted impact after verified analysis.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Mid-run newly shared file triggers coordination before merge, no runaway agent loop.
- [ ] External branch updates mark stale manifests; failed planner preserves code and scheduling resumes deterministically.
- [ ] No false Ready/complete on pause or restart.
## Dependencies
Blocked by manifest, analyzer, coordination and scheduler siblings; integrates #131 #178 and #127.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Implementation code + schema/API docs and local test commands committed.
- [ ] Relevant deterministic unit/integration tests and failure fixtures pass.
- [ ] Existing owner integrations preserved, no duplicate scheduling/ledger services.
- [ ] Link PR, validation evidence and rollout/feature-flag behavior to this issue.

All compute runs on locally managed workers; no GitHub Actions compute.
